title: Dispatch: olc5.7 pack-side typed proficiency grants (attempt 1)
description:
Pack-side typed proficiency grants for eshyra-olc5.7 (read its DESIGN field: decision D1 is this task). Importer work: follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md exactly (no hand edits of records.json; regenerate; explain every generated diff).

WHAT TO BUILD
1. packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/mechanicsProjections.ts
   - The typed-proficiency grammar near L4645 ("const proficiency = ... /\b[Yy]ou (?:have|gain) proficiency (with|in) ([^.]+)\./") currently emits {kind:'proficiency', grant:<verbatim>}. Add a pure helper (e.g. typeProficiencyGrant(grant: string)) that returns optional typed fields ONLY when the WHOLE grant phrase is one of these shapes (case-insensitive, allow a leading 'the'):
       '<Ability> saving throws'                    -> savingThrows:['wisdom']   (Ability in Strength|Dexterity|Constitution|Intelligence|Wisdom|Charisma; lowercase output)
       '<Skill> skill' / '<Skill> and <Skill> skills' / '<A>, <B>, and <C> skills' -> skills:[canonical names]  (canonical = the 18 SRD skills exactly as spelled in feature:college-of-lore:bonus-proficiencies data.choices[0].from, e.g. 'Animal Handling', 'Sleight of Hand')
       '<light|medium|heavy> armor' / 'shields' (and comma/and lists of those) -> armor:['heavy armor'] etc. (lowercase, values limited to 'light armor','medium armor','heavy armor','shields')
     Anything else (weapons, tools, languages, 'three skills of your choice', conditional grants) -> no typed fields. Keep `grant` verbatim always. Do NOT add typed fields to the conditional-expertise proficiency branch (~L4630, it has a condition).
   - Diamond Soul branch (~L4838, /(?:gain|grants you) proficiency in all saving throws/): keep scope:'all-saving-throws' and add savingThrows with all six abilities in order strength,dexterity,constitution,intelligence,wisdom,charisma.
   - Expected effects: feature:rogue:slippery-mind -> {kind:'proficiency', grant:'Wisdom saving throws', savingThrows:['wisdom']}; feature:life-domain:bonus-proficiency -> {..., grant:'heavy armor', armor:['heavy armor']}; feature:college-of-lore:bonus-proficiencies unchanged (grant 'three skills of your choice' is a choice, not a fixed grant). Ancestry/other records that match a typed shape (e.g. a trait 'You have proficiency in the Perception skill') will incidentally gain skills:[...] — that is a source-confirmed incidental consequence of the same fix; list every such record in your report. Magic items do NOT go through this function? -> verify; magicItemPassiveEffects.ts emits its own literal {kind:'proficiency', grant} objects; leave those untouched.
2. Option-level grants: Eldritch Invocation options are built in deriveFeatureChoices.ts (or wherever choices[].options[] {id,name,text,source} are assembled; find it). For each option, run ONLY the typed proficiency grammar over option.text; when it yields typed fields, attach option.mechanics = {effects:[{kind:'proficiency', grant:<verbatim>, ...typed}]}. Expected: eldritch-invocation:beguiling-influence gets {kind:'proficiency', grant:'the Deception and Persuasion skills', skills:['Deception','Persuasion']} (grant text = exactly what the regex captures; keep whatever the existing grammar would capture, including or excluding 'the' consistently with feature records). No other option should change; if another does, verify it against its text and report it.
3. Types/schema: packages/core/src/rules/featureChoices.ts FeatureChoiceOption gains readonly mechanics?: { readonly effects: readonly ProficiencyGrantEffect[] } (define the effect type with grant: string and optional savingThrows/skills/armor). packages/core/src/rules/kindSchemas.ts: the 'proficiency' effect validator (find where effect kinds are validated; there is a per-kind validator map like proficiencyBonusIncrease at ~L3698) must accept and VALIDATE the optional typed fields (savingThrows subset of the six abilities, skills subset of the 18 canonical skills, armor subset of the four values, each non-empty, no duplicates); the feature-choice option validator must accept the optional mechanics with only proficiency effects. Reject unknown values (fail closed). Field provenance: if tests fail because new fields need declarations (fieldProvenanceDeclarations.ts / source-region ledger excludes derived mechanics subtrees), follow the existing pattern for derived mechanics.
4. Regenerate: npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1 (see the importer README for the .generated copy too), then npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack must exit 0. Diff records.json and list every changed record key.
5. Tests (generalized, proportionate; put them beside existing mechanicsProjections/importer tests under packages/core/test/importers/):
   - unit table for typeProficiencyGrant: positive shapes above + negatives ('three skills of your choice', 'the battleaxe, handaxe, light hammer, and warhammer', 'thieves' tools', 'Wisdom saving throws if you are ...' style condition, an unknown skill name) -> no typed fields.
   - one pack-level invariant over the REAL committed pack: every proficiency effect (feature records and choice options) that carries typed fields has typed values that appear verbatim-equivalent in its `grant` text (e.g. each skill name occurs in grant; each ability name occurs in grant or scope is all-saving-throws), and the four named records carry exactly the expected typed values. Do not write one test per record beyond those four.
   - kindSchemas validator: rejects an unknown skill / ability / armor value.
DO NOT: touch docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/freeze-manifest.json or add thaw notes; touch engine/character code (that is child .2); run other projectors on option text.
HARD STOP: If the failure map reveals a new root cause, requires a new parser or extractor strategy, or creates generated churn outside the direct consequences of the current minimal fix, stop and report instead of broadening the implementation. Do not add complexity solely to suppress source-confirmed incidental improvements caused by the correct fix; verify, test where practical, and list them.
